question: What sideways tilt must the bus withstand on a tilt rig without tipping over?
answer: It must not reach the overturning point when the platform is tilted to 28° from horizontal, to each side in turn.
notes: [review] OK. Optional wording fix: 'What sideways tilt must the bus withstand on a tilt rig without tipping over?' (current phrasing implies rolling over is allowed past the limit). Rewording applied.

question: What are the minimum height and width of an emergency door opening on a full-size bus of Class I, II or III?
answer: At least 1,450 mm high and 600 mm wide.
notes: [review] OK.

question: If a power-operated door closes on someone, how much squeezing force is tolerated before it has to reopen?
answer: The door must reopen fully when resisted by a clamping force of no more than 150 N; a brief peak above 150 N is allowed as long as it stays under 300 N.
notes: [review] OK.

question: Какая минимальная освещённость нужна на полу прохода, когда работает аварийное освещение салона?
answer: Не менее 1 люкса на уровне пола по осевой линии проходов и проходов к дверям, а также в центре каждой ступени (сама система аварийного освещения обязательна для классов II, III и B).
notes: Related: 10 lux at 750 mm height is in 7.8.3.7 but the question asks about floor level. [review] Correct; added class-scope clause to answer (7.8.3 lead-in).

question: What is the minimum seat pitch between rows of forward-facing seats in an intercity coach (Class II or III)?
answer: 680 mm, measured horizontally from the front of one seat back to the back of the seat in front (650 mm for Classes I, A and B).
notes: The regulation calls this 'seat spacing' (dimension H). [review] OK.

question: How big does the dedicated area for one wheelchair user inside the bus have to be?
answer: At least 750 mm wide, 1,300 mm long and 1,400 mm high, aligned with the vehicle's longitudinal axis.
notes: [review] OK.

question: What minimum platform size and rated load does a wheelchair lift need?
answer: The platform must be at least 800 mm wide and 1,200 mm long and work with a load of at least 300 kg.
notes: [review] OK.

question: How steep may a wheelchair ramp be when deployed to a 150 mm kerb, and when deployed straight to the road?
answer: Not more than 12 % onto a 150 mm kerb and not more than 36 % to the ground; kneeling may be used to achieve this.
notes: [review] OK (text says 'should not exceed').

question: At what earth leakage level does a trolleybus have to isolate itself from the overhead wires on its own?
answer: When the leakage current between chassis and road exceeds 3 mA or the leakage voltage exceeds 60 V DC (disconnection applies when the trolleybus is stationary).
notes: [review] OK. Same gold as h003 — near-duplicate coverage of 4.3.

question: During the re-ignition test of an engine-bay fire extinguishing system, how long must the fire stay out?
answer: No re-ignition is allowed for 45 seconds after the fire has been completely put out.
notes: Same 45 s requirement appears for component approval (Part 1) and for a specific engine compartment (Part 2); both listed. [review] OK.

question: What is the maximum height of the first step above the road at the service door of a Class III coach?
answer: 380 mm for at least one service door (400 mm for other service doors; 430 mm if the vehicle has purely mechanical suspension).
notes: Answer is in the Figure 8 table and footnotes (Annex 4, p. 84, read from PDF). If the coach is fitted for reduced-mobility access, Annex 8 3.1 imposes 320 mm for at least one door; question is about the general limit. [review] OK, footnotes 2/3 match.

question: When the bus is fully loaded, what share of its maximum mass has to rest on the driven axle(s)?
answer: At least 25 % of the technically permissible maximum laden mass M.
notes: [review] OK.

question: What qualifies a bus as 'low floor' under UN R107?
answer: A Class I, II or A vehicle where at least 35 % of the standing area (front section for articulated, lower deck for double-deckers) is step-free and includes access to at least one service door.
notes: [review] OK.

question: Что означает «Класс II» для автобусов по Правилам ООН № 107?
answer: Автобус вместимостью более 22 пассажиров, предназначенный в основном для сидящих пассажиров; стоящие допускаются только в проходе и/или на площади не больше, чем занимают два двойных сиденья.
notes: [review] OK (>22 comes from 2.1.1 lead-in).

question: What does the regulation mean by the superstructure of a bus body?
answer: The part of the bodywork that contributes to the vehicle's strength in a roll-over accident.
notes: [review] Answer softened: text says 'contributes to the strength', not 'gives the vehicle its strength'.

question: Which voltage range puts a trolleybus circuit into Class B?
answer: Rated voltage above 30 V up to 1,000 V AC, and above 60 V up to 1,500 V DC.
notes: The ≤ signs are dropped in blocks.jsonl text; confirmed from the rendered PDF page 129. [review] OK.

question: For trolleybus electrics, how is basic insulation different from supplementary insulation?
answer: Basic insulation protects people from electrical hazards in systems that have protective bonding; supplementary insulation does so in systems without protective bonding. Together they form double insulation.
notes: [review] Added 1.5.4 to gold: the 'double insulation' sentence in the answer is supported only there.

question: Кого Правила относят к пассажирам с ограниченной мобильностью?
answer: Всех, кому трудно пользоваться общественным транспортом: инвалидов (включая колясочников, людей с сенсорными и интеллектуальными нарушениями, нарушениями конечностей), людей маленького роста, пожилых, беременных, пассажиров с тяжёлым багажом, тележками для покупок или с детьми, в том числе в колясках.
notes: [review] OK.

question: Does R107 cover buses built specifically to take children to school?
answer: No. Vehicles specially designed for carrying school children are excluded from the regulation's requirements.
notes: [review] OK.

question: We are building a mobile library on a bus chassis. Do we have to meet all of R107?
answer: Only as far as the requirements are compatible with its use, provided it carries no more than 8 people (excluding the driver) while moving; the seats used while driving must be clearly identified.
notes: [review] OK.

question: We're building a minibus for about 20 people with the motor at the back. Is a self-triggering extinguisher under the motor cover compulsory, or is a heat warning for the driver enough?
answer: A heat warning is enough. With the engine (or a combustion heater) behind the driver's compartment, an over-temperature alarm with acoustic and visual signal is required; a fire suppression system is mandatory only for Classes I, II and III and optional for Classes A and B (≤22 passengers).
notes: Applies to vehicles with a combustion engine or combustion heater behind the driver's compartment. [review] Leakage fix: removed 'Class A or B', 'engine bay', 'fire suppression'. Answer verified.

question: Обязана ли быть система аварийного освещения в городском автобусе класса I?
answer: Нет. Обязательна она только для классов II, III и B; для класса I не требуется.
notes: [review] Removed parenthetical about fire alarm: it was supported only by 7.5.7.1(a), which is not in gold and applies only to rear-engined vehicles.

question: Can a trolleybus have emergency escape hatches in its roof?
answer: No. Roof escape hatches are prohibited on trolleybuses.
notes: 7.6.1.12 (no hatches near high-voltage systems) is related but the explicit trolleybus ban is in 7.6.1.11. [review] OK.

question: Do intercity and long-distance coaches have to be wheelchair accessible, or is that only for city buses?
answer: Only Class I must accommodate a wheelchair user (and one pram/pushchair). For other classes accessibility is left to the Contracting Parties, but any accessibility features that are fitted must comply with Annex 8.
notes: [review] Wording narrowed from 'only Class I must be accessible': Annex 3 7.7.8.5.3 still requires 2 priority seats in Class II, so Class II has some mandatory reduced-mobility provisions.

question: Does the driver's seat in a Class B minibus need a suspension and height adjustment?
answer: No. Suspension and vertical adjustment are required in general but are not mandatory for Classes A and B; fore-aft and backrest adjustment with automatic locking still apply.
notes: [review] Added 7.7.14.7.1 explicitly to gold: the 'No' lives there; if chunks split at that level, 7.7.14.7 alone gives the opposite answer.

question: How steep can the aisle be in a city bus compared with a touring coach, and is the wheelchair route held to a tighter limit?
answer: Lengthwise: 8 % for Classes I, II, A and 12.5 % for Classes III and B; crosswise 5 % for all. The path from a wheelchair space to an entrance/exit is limited to 5 % (8 % from priority seats).
notes: [review] OK. Minor: 3.5 allows exceedance where differently directed slopes merge (≤25 % of swept area).

question: In the hybrid (static plus dynamic) test route for wheelchair tie-downs, how do the static loads on the floor anchorages differ between M2 and M3 buses?
answer: M2: 1,110 ± 20 daN forward and 550 ± 20 daN rearward. M3: 740 ± 20 daN forward and 370 ± 20 daN rearward. In both cases applied 200–300 mm above the wheelchair space floor.
notes: Hybrid-test anchorages (3.8.3); the static-test route in 3.8.2 has different values. [review] Question disambiguated: 3.8.2.2 also tests 'restraint system and its anchorages' (1,715/1,130 daN forward at 45°, 810 daN rearward), so the old wording had two valid answers.

question: Насколько меньше может быть аварийная дверь у микроавтобуса класса A или B по сравнению с большим автобусом?
answer: Для классов I–III проём не менее 1 450 × 600 мм; для классов A и B по альтернативным требованиям — 1 250 × 550 мм, а ширина может уменьшаться до 300 мм у колёсных арок при сохранении 550 мм на высоте от 400 мм.
notes: Annex 7 table is in blocks with section null under heading 1.1 (p. 105). [review] OK. Not covered: Annex 7 1.1.1 allows 1,100 × 550 mm for Class B ≤3.5 t with ≤12 seats (Annex 3 7.7.1.10).

question: If the first attempt of a fire extinguishing test fails, what retest rule applies for a component-approved system versus one approved for a specific engine bay?
answer: In substance the same rule: a pass on the first attempt is enough; if the first attempt fails, the second and third attempts must both succeed. Part 1 words it as 'two of three attempts' (with the first failed, that means attempts 2 and 3), Part 2 states it directly.
notes: Same rule repeated for low-load, fan and re-ignition tests (Part 1 1.4.3/1.5.3/1.6.3; Part 2 1.5.3/1.6.3/1.7.3). [review] ANSWER WAS WRONG: old gold answer claimed a difference that does not exist logically. Consider dropping as a comparison item or keeping as a 'trick' comparison with a no-difference answer.

question: What distinguishes a Class A minibus from a Class B one?
answer: Both carry up to 22 passengers. Class A has seats plus provision for standing passengers; Class B has no provision for standees.
notes: [review] OK.

question: When proving that a city bus won't tip over on a side-tilt platform, what weight stands in for each person sitting down?
answer: A mass Q per seat; for Class I (and A) Q is 68 kg (71 kg for Classes II, III and B, including 3 kg of hand baggage).
notes: The Q table is printed on p. 125 directly after 3.2.3.2.1; in blocks.jsonl the table rows have section_number null. If chunks attribute it differently, gold may need page 125. [review] Leakage fix: removed 'ballast', 'each passenger seat', 'tilt test'. Answer verified.

question: Where on a power-operated door should the anti-pinch force be measured?
answer: At the main closing edges: one point in the middle of the door and one 150 mm above its lower edge (plus the most dangerous point of secondary edges if anti-clamping for opening is fitted); the limit checked is 150 N.
notes: [review] OK.

question: Какой контраст должны иметь кнопки связи с водителем у приоритетных мест и по какой формуле он считается?
answer: Контраст C ≥ 0,4 и диффузное отражение не менее 0,5 (либо кнопка белая или жёлтая). C = |ρ1 − ρ2| / (ρ1 + ρ2), где ρ1 — отражение материала объекта, ρ2 — окружающей поверхности.
notes: Formula symbols (ρ) are dropped in blocks.jsonl; formula confirmed from the rendered PDF page 101. [review] OK.

question: How do people at a stop know a bus can take someone in a wheelchair: what sign has to be on the bodywork, and how big must it be?
answer: The wheelchair-user pictogram (Figure 23A): white symbol on blue, at least 130 mm in diameter, shown on the front nearside and next to the relevant service door(s), plus one inside at each wheelchair space.
notes: [review] Leakage fix: removed 'wheelchair space', 'displayed on the outside', 'symbol'. 'wheelchair' itself is unavoidable. Answer verified.

question: Our extinguishing system was type-approved as a component. How do we size it for a rear engine bay with 6 m³ gross volume?
answer: The component's documented agent mass and discharge points refer to a 4 m³ compartment. Above 4 m³ scale up with Sx = 0.1·x + 0.6, i.e. 1.2 for 6 m³: about 20 % more agent mass, discharge points (rounded to the nearest whole number), propellant gas container mass and discharge tube length, at the same system pressure. Gross volume is used (engine volume not subtracted) and includes any combustion heater compartments.
notes: Annex 1 item; 4 m³ reference also in 2.4/2.5 of that appendix. [review] Answer made precise: text scales the propellant gas *container* mass and the discharge tube length; added rounding rule.

question: Сколько приоритетных мест нужно в автобусе класса I и на какой высоте должен идти поручень от них до двери?
answer: Не менее четырёх приоритетных мест; поручень на высоте 800–900 мм от пола между ними и хотя бы одной служебной дверью, разрывы не более 1 050 мм с вертикальным поручнем хотя бы с одной стороны разрыва.
notes: [review] OK.

question: What turning circle does a bus need to be able to fit inside?
answer: It must complete a full 360° circle on either side within a ring between an outer radius of 12.5 m and an inner radius of 5.3 m.
notes: Document says 'manoeuvrability' and 'concentric circles', never 'turning circle'. [review] OK.

question: Can we put movie screens for passengers where the driver can see them?
answer: No. Passenger entertainment displays must be outside the driver's view from the normal driving position; screens used by the driver for operating the vehicle (e.g. door monitoring) are allowed.
notes: [review] OK.

question: How high can the stop-request buttons be mounted in a city bus?
answer: Generally no higher than 1,500 mm above the floor (extra higher ones may be added), operable with the palm and spread evenly through the vehicle. Because a city (Class I) bus must meet Annex 8, buttons next to priority seats and in wheelchair areas must be 700–1,200 mm high, and those in low-floor areas without seats 800–1,500 mm.
notes: Document says 'communication devices' / 'signal that the driver should stop'. [review] ANSWER WAS INCOMPLETE: Class I is always subject to Annex 8 (Reg. 5.2), which adds tighter height bands. Added Annex 8 3.3.1/3.3.2 to gold.

question: Does every glass break-out window need an emergency hammer next to it?
answer: Yes, for emergency windows of readily-breakable safety glass a breaking device must be provided next to each one; for rear windows it goes centrally above or below, or one at each end.
notes: Document never says 'hammer'. [review] OK.

question: Можно ли ехать, если автобус ещё «присевший» на остановке?
answer: Только медленно: пока кузов опущен ниже нормальной дорожной высоты, система не должна позволять двигаться быстрее 5 км/ч.
notes: Colloquial 'присевший' for kneeling system. [review] OK.

question: How much clearance is needed between combustible trim and hot parts like the tailpipe or turbo?
answer: No flammable material within 100 mm of exhaust components, high-voltage equipment or other significant heat sources unless it is effectively shielded.
notes: Requirement text is an unnumbered block directly under heading 7.5.5 (p. 47). [review] OK.

question: What is the maximum overall length allowed for an articulated city bus?
notes: Annex 11 only defines how length is measured (ISO 612) and requires the turning-circle test; no length limit. Searched 'maximum length', '18.75', '12.0 m': no hits except service-door lighting zone. [review] Confirmed unanswerable. Hard negatives: Annex 11 2.2.1, 3.4.1, 3.4.4 (manufacturer-declared max dimensions for incomplete vehicles).

question: What is the test procedure for checking the strength of the bus body in a rollover?
notes: Only the definition of superstructure (Reg 2.4) mentions roll-over; no test. Searched 'roll-over', 'rollover', 'Regulation No. 66'. Retrieval may surface 2.4 — it does not answer. [review] Confirmed. Strong hard negative: Annex 3 7.4 + Annex 3 Appendix (static tilt stability, 'overturning') — that is stability, not body strength.

question: What is the maximum allowed interior noise level at the driver's seat?
notes: Searched 'noise', 'dB': no hits. [review] Confirmed. Only near-miss: 'sound-proofing material' (Annex 3 7.5.1.1, fire rule).

question: Are there thermal runaway requirements for the traction battery of a battery-electric bus?
notes: Searched 'REESS', 'thermal runaway', 'traction batter', 'rechargeable': none. Annex 3 7.5.3 has generic battery mounting/ventilation rules and Annex 12 3.6 battery case materials for trolleybuses, neither addresses thermal runaway. [review] Confirmed. Also hard negative: Annex 1 Part 1 App. 1 item 6.5 (trolleybus autonomous-service battery/supercaps — information fields only).

question: Какой максимальный тормозной путь допускается для автобуса категории M3?
notes: Braking performance is not covered. Searched 'braking distance', 'Regulation No. 13'; 'braking' only appears as a load case (heavy braking) for guards and staircases. [review] Confirmed. Also hard negative: Annex 8 3.8.3.8 (deceleration pulse 48–50 km/h for wheelchair restraint sled test).

question: At what speed must the speed limiter be set on a long-distance coach?
notes: Searched 'speed limit', 'Regulation No. 89': none. Speeds in the text (3, 5, 20 km/h) relate to doors, steps, kneeling — not limiters. [review] Confirmed. Also hard negative: Annex 1 item 6.2.6 'Maximum velocity' (trolleybus info field).

question: Какая минимальная остаточная глубина протектора шин допускается у автобуса?
notes: Searched 'tread depth', 'tyre tread': none ('tread' only as step tread). [review] Confirmed. Near-miss: 'tyre equipment and pressure' in Annex 3 7.7.7.2/7.7.7.3 (step height measurement).

question: What fresh-air flow per passenger does the HVAC system have to supply?
notes: Searched 'ventilat', 'air-condition', 'air condition': only battery compartment ventilation (Annex 3 7.5.3.2). No passenger ventilation requirement. [review] Confirmed. Note the literal token 'HVAC' does occur (Annex 1 item 6.2.4, trolleybus rated line current incl. HVAC) — lexical hard negative; also 7.7.13.4 demisting and Annex 13 fan air flow 1.5 m³/s.

question: Must there be a first aid kit on a trolleybus?
answer: R107 requires space for fitting one or more first-aid kits (at least 7 dm3, smallest dimension at least 80 mm); it applies to all vehicles including trolleybuses. Whether a kit must actually be carried is not set by R107.
notes: Author's original answer was 'Yes'; text requires space for the kit, not the kit itself. [review] OK.

question: Is it acceptable for the aisle floor to rise 1 in 10 from front to back?
answer: Depends on the class: max 8% for Classes I, II and A (so no), max 12.5% for Classes III and B (so yes).
notes: [review] Leakage fix: removed 'slope', 'longitudinal direction', '10%'. Caveat: if Annex 8 features are fitted, the route to a wheelchair space is ≤5 % and to priority seats ≤8 % (Annex 8 3.5), so 'yes' for Class III/B holds only outside those routes.

question: Must a trolleybus be equipped with a leakage current and insulation monitoring device?
answer: Leakage monitoring: yes — an onboard device must permanently monitor leakage current or voltage between chassis and road and disconnect the high-voltage circuits (when stationary) above 3 mA or 60 V DC. A permanent insulation-monitoring device is not required: R107 only requires means for periodic insulation-resistance tests (≥10 MΩ at 1,000 V DC), and the information document lists insulation monitoring as 'if any'.
notes: [review] ANSWER WAS OVERCLAIMED: 'Yes' covered the insulation-monitoring half too, which the text does not mandate (Annex 1 item 6.2.11 'Insulation monitoring (if any)'). Added Annex 12 3.9 to gold. Overlaps q009.
